questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had previously been to Colombia and I really like the culture, the nature, the history and its current situation of being a middle income country and the challenges it faces.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Although all information was sent out quite late, we could always ask Anderson (the guy responsible for exchange) if we had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received some guide by email on how to do everything we needed to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don't live to far from campus, it will be annoying

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found housing in a complex meant for students at Uniandes. It was quite expensive for local standards, but there were guards and it was nice to have shops closeby without having to leave the complex, especially at night

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's quite easy. Guides were sent out before registration and they are attentive on the day of registration, as it is first come, first serve.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration happened couple of weeks before the start of the semester online. The courses with prerequisites were handled through one system, and the others through another system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They were physically able to help in a room on campus, and online through Teams

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every class i applied for, but some of the courses from earlier years were not offered, which was a bummer.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be flexible. Register more courses than you need, as you can start on more courses than necessary and drop out of the ones you like the least

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Similar to KU, maybe a bit lower, although students didn't seem to do as much work.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. More similar to STX; attendance is obligatory and assignements and presentations throughout the semester count towards the final grade

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economía social,  Seminario Economía, política social, equidad y pobreza,  Economía Marxista and Español Lengua Extranjera 4

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the seminar. The spanish course is really nice. I couldn't attend the summer course, but I would recommend it if you're not completely confident in your spanish

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I ate out almost always at least twice a day (at not the cheapest options), as the shared kitchen always was dirty. As such, I had extremely high cost of food. You could easily spend only 1500 DKK even eating out once a day. I travelled more than I expected, so that's the high personal spending as well

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Hmm, maybe travelling. Flight tickets were quite expensive last minute.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The sports and dance lessons are really good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of events for exchange students and some events were for all students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports or dance. They have a lot of different sports or dance classes free of charge at the uni

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Colombia is so diverse, you're not gonna have time enough to explore this amazing country in only one semester ;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, but I really miss being able to walk on the streets alone at night - after dark, you shouldn't walk alone in the streets. I didn't get mugged or anything stolen, but a lot of the students did - some with knife. Be careful, and you'll be fine, and I wouldn't let this fact get in the way of going, it's no different than other Latin American countries.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmm, the food. As a vegetarian, it might be a bit more dificult, although in Bogotá it was very easy. The cafeteria always had a vegetarian menu, but when travelling outside, it becomes more dificult... Prepare to get tired of colombian food ;)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness, dancing, night life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it and choose courses where you have friday and/or monday off, so you can travel

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Colombian bureaucracy is a real thing - have patience and be stern. People who complain get their will, which is a bit a shame, but it's true

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, becoming fluent in Spanish, learning about colombian society, history and challenges

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not moving my body enough - in DK I bike everywhere I go and go for walks. Here, I had to actively go to the gym, which didn't happen as often as I wanted to

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
